title: Called-Due Appraisal Charge in Retention Payoff Approvals
content:
**Called-due appraisal charge — Payoff and Loan Satisfaction.** On the payoff case of a Borrower Voluntary Payoff requested by the borrower of record on a loan whose maturity case is due and payable, in its extension period or referred to foreclosure, the called-due appraisal charge that enters the retention balance figure is USD 650.00 for a two-to-four-unit property and USD 550.00 for an FHA-approved condominium or manufactured-home property, as recorded on the loan under the Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM) product. Every other property, and a Summit loan, which records no property type, takes no adjustment under this rule.

### Basis questions

**Which record decides the amount?** The property type on the HECM loan record.

**Does a condominium always take USD 550.00?** An FHA-approved condominium does; the rule names that property type.

**What does a two-to-four-unit property take?** USD 650.00.

**Is a Summit loan affected?** No. A Summit loan records no property type and takes no adjustment under this rule.

| Hypothetical property | Called-due appraisal charge under this rule |
|---|---|
| HECM on a three-unit home | USD 650.00 |
| HECM on a manufactured home | USD 550.00 |
| HECM on a detached single-family home | no adjustment under this rule |
